summary: Across 2014 to 2023, Olivia Chow's posts frame civic engagement as a collective, participatory practice. Chow has repeatedly encouraged voting, urging Ontarians and Torontonians to cast ballots and to "vote for what you believe in" rather than out of fear (uGINR0utA2, t-5vGnutPZ, pJp-RlutGb), and modeled the behavior by voting early herself (CtUbO-FgORx, uqSun1OtKe). Chow has emphasized community-based consultation, citing direct outreach to Flemingdon families on the Science Centre (CrPADE5p7N1, Cr9aUuAtQRF) and canvassing on women's issues (8qjgVJutDR). Chow has expressed solidarity with labour, 2SLGBTQI+, Sikh, and Indigenous communities (Csrr8tmPhyK, Ct422Chv9qe, Cr9ZV3pvq-u, 0wB8t1OtIm), and has framed democratic strength as collective: "not just about one mayor... all of us together" (Cs7bZwhgbZj, CuAqVppPbav).

key_positions.stance: Encourages voter participation in elections at all levels
Frames democracy as a collective effort beyond any single official
Supports direct community consultation in civic decision-making
Expresses solidarity with marginalized and equity-seeking communities (2SLGBTQI+, Sikh, working people, Indigenous women)
Views Pride and community-building as inherently political
Supports neighbourhood-level cultural and learning spaces outside the downtown core

key_actions.action: Cast ballot in early voting for 2023 Toronto mayoral by-election
Voted in the 2014 Toronto municipal election with her granddaughters
Consulted Flemingdon Park families about the future of the Ontario Science Centre
Stood with OPSEU/SEFPO workers and Thorncliffe/Flemingdon residents opposing relocation of the Ontario Science Centre
Joined a Spadina–Fort York rally against Bill C-51
Canvassed in Spadina–Fort York on women's issues
Served as observer for Tunisia's first free presidential election
Presented the first Jack Layton Progress Prize to Fay Blaney of the Women's Memorial March Committee
Spoke with media alongside MPPs Tabuns and DiNovo about John Tory's agenda
Met with Bloomberg to discuss gridlock, affordable housing, and Toronto's global profile
